The driver's only stated reason is an external traffic cause - 'in this jam'. Tested as POL-RD-13 requires, against the traffic_advisory for this trip and nothing else, that assertion fails: the bundle's sole advisory, EV-ADVIS-00715-01, is MISSING, carrying no payload, status MISSING, weight_multiplier 0.0 and issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT. Nothing in the rider's profile burdens her claim: rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 0 and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0, so the POL-RD-08 corroboration trigger - 4 or more claims with 1 or fewer substantiated - does not fire and no corroboration beyond the gps_trace is demanded of her. The trip is upfront-quoted: charged_total (7.20) equals quoted_fare_sgd (7.20), and there is no properly chargeable ERP, toll, surcharge or waiting-time line, so POL-RD-11(a) computes to 0.00 - the fare artifact itself publishes pol_rd_11_remedy 0.00. POL-RD-02 does not run on an upfront trip, and POL-RD-09(4) finds no phantom gantry line and no misplaced surcharge. Taken alone, the route-deviation money clauses return the rider nothing.

Because no monetary clause reaches the proven facts, the rider's entitlement is genuinely unresolved on this record and the case should ESCALATE under POL-RD-10 rather than close against her. POL-RD-01's gate tests for excess and has no reading for a negative excess; POL-RD-11 returns zero on an upfront fare; and the driver's admitted abandonment of the journey (EV-CHAT-00715) is remedied by no clause at all. I note that POL-RD-13(1) removes the missing advisory as a POL-RD-10(5) trigger, since the driver cited no advisory identifier, so the escalation rests on POL-RD-10(1): no ruling can be made at or above the 0.70 confidence floor where no monetary clause fits these facts. Here the trace covers 3.4 km against a 6.4 km optimal route, an excess of -3.0 km (derived excess_pct -46.875%): the vehicle drove less far than the optimal route, so neither establishment test can pass and no deviation exists. Under POL-RD-01 the outcome is NO_ACTION however the rider characterises the trip.

POL-RD-01 makes gps_trace.trace_distance_km the governing measurement where it differs from the rounded trip_record convenience copy, and the trace-derived deviation status is expressly 'no deviation'. There is no admissible measurement in this bundle on which the rider can clear the POL-RD-01 threshold.

The rider carries the initial burden under POL-RD-08 and must show an excess meeting the POL-RD-01 threshold, measured from a gps_trace that is not impaired under POL-RD-07(a) to (c). The trace is unimpaired - 100% coverage, 55 fixes at a 10 s cadence, no gaps and a maximum gap of 0.0 s - yet it discloses no excess at all. The burden is never discharged and the driver is never put to an exculpatory clause.

This trip is UPFRONT_QUOTE with a quoted_fare_sgd of 7.20, so under POL-RD-11 the POL-RD-02 distance-and-time recomputation does not run and no distance-or-time refund is available to the rider however the trip is characterised. The only route-deviation remedy is the POL-RD-11(a) amount by which charged_total exceeds the quote: charged_total is SGD 7.20, the quoted fare is SGD 7.20, and the properly chargeable pass-through and statutory lines total SGD 0.00, so the remedy computes to SGD 0.00.

Nothing in the fare engages the POL-RD-09 pass-through and billing-integrity corrections: there are no ERP gantry lines (total SGD 0.00), no airport surcharge - the trip ends at a shelter and does not originate at an airport - and a waiting-time fee of SGD 0.00. With no off-route or phantom line, POL-RD-09(4) is not triggered and no standalone refund or billing-integrity referral arises.

The only chat message is the driver's own note that he would end the trip; it records no rider instruction and no departure from the optimal corridor. It describes a trip cut short, which the trace corroborates - 3.4 km driven against a 6.4 km optimal route - and route deviation provides no refund for a trip driven under its optimal distance. The message changes none of the arithmetic under POL-RD-01 or POL-RD-11.

Even if POL-RD-06 were consulted, no repeat-deviation pattern is established: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against driver_profile.completed_trips_90d of 250, below both the count-of-three gate and the 0.05 ratio gate. POL-RD-06 is in any event not triggered, because no material deviation is recorded on this trip.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider and to the driver: I have decided this case on the route-deviation policy, which is the category it was filed under, and every figure below is read off the record so both of you can check it.

The governing measurement is the GPS trace. EV-GPS-00715 is unimpaired — 100% coverage, 55 fixes at the published 10-second cadence, no gaps and a maximum gap of 0.0 s — so no POL-RD-07 issue arises and nothing has to be reconstructed across a gap. The trace shows the vehicle covered 3.4 km (trace_distance_km) against a booked optimal route of 6.4 km (trip_record.optimal_distance_km). The excess is 3.4 − 6.4 = −3.0 km, i.e. −46.9%. POL-RD-01 establishes a deviation only where the excess is greater than 20% of the optimal distance and greater than 0.8 km; a negative excess fails both tests, so no deviation exists and the clause directs NO_ACTION however the trip is characterised.

That closes the distance-and-time route. This was an upfront-quoted trip (fare_model UPFRONT_QUOTE on EV-FARE-00715), so POL-RD-02 does not run and no distance-or-time refund is available. The only route-deviation money is the POL-RD-11(a) amount by which charged_total exceeds the quote plus the properly chargeable pass-through and statutory lines. Charged_total is SGD 7.20, quoted_fare_sgd is SGD 7.20, and there are no ERP gantry lines (SGD 0.00), no airport surcharge, and a waiting-time fee of SGD 0.00, so that amount computes to SGD 0.00 — the fare artifact itself publishes pol_rd_11_remedy 0.00. I have also checked POL-RD-09: with no charge line the trace never crossed and no surcharge on a trip that does not originate at an airport, there is no billing-integrity correction and no POL-RD-09(4) referral.

The rider's account of what happened is not in dispute and I accept it. The driver's own in-app message at 12:25:40, "Hospital too far in this jam. I will end here and refund you.", and the trip record's dropoff label, "Shelter where service ended", show the trip was ended short of the hospital. But no clause in this policy turns an unfinished trip into a refund: the route-deviation clauses measure excess over the optimal route, not distance left undriven, and the upfront rules fix the fare at booking and close the distance-and-time route. The driver's "in this jam" explanation does him no good either — the only traffic advisory for the trip, EV-ADVIS-00715-01, is MISSING with weight 0.0 and issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, so POL-RD-03 cannot be run on this record and, per POL-RD-13, an uncited traffic assertion carries no weight under POL-RD-08. Nothing here decides against the rider's honesty; the route-deviation rules simply provide no money for these facts.

No clause in this policy produces a referral, and no POL-RD-10 escalation trigger fires: the trip identifiers match across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown, the trace is unimpaired, no timestamps conflict, no exculpatory clause has been invoked against a cited artifact, and no charge line lacks a counterpart. The disputed SGD 7.20 therefore stands as charged: fare_breakdown.payment_status (CHARGED) and refund_issued_sgd (0.00) are left as they are.

One open question, which belongs here rather than in any referral: the record shows you were carried 3.4 km of a 6.4 km journey and charged the full upfront fare of SGD 7.20, and the driver told you in writing that a refund was coming. That may well be worth pursuing, but it is not a route deviation and this policy gives me no power over it. If you wish to take it further, raise it directly with support as a trip-completion or service dispute.

To the rider: I accept that the driver ended your trip before the hospital. The driver's own in-app message (EV-CHAT-00715) reads 'Hospital too far in this jam. I will end here and refund you.', and the trip record's dropoff is 'Shelter where service ended'. But this dispute was filed as a route deviation, and on the evidence there is no route deviation to refund.

POL-RD-01 defines a deviation only where the distance actually driven exceeds the booked optimal route by more than 20% and by more than 0.8 km. The governing measurement is the GPS trace (EV-GPS-00715): 3.4 km driven against a 6.4 km optimal route, an excess of -3.0 km (-46.875%). The vehicle drove less far than the optimal route, so neither establishment test passes and no deviation exists. POL-RD-01 directs NO_ACTION however the trip is characterised, and the category gives no refund for a trip driven under its optimal distance.

The fare closes the other route to a refund. EV-FARE-00715 is an upfront quote (fare_model UPFRONT_QUOTE; quoted_fare_sgd 7.20; total_charged 7.20; refund_issued_sgd 0.00). Under POL-RD-11 the distance and time charges were fixed at booking and POL-RD-02 does not run; the only route-deviation remedies are the amount by which charged_total exceeds the quote plus properly chargeable pass-throughs, and a POL-RD-09 pass-through correction. Both are SGD 0.00 here: charged_total 7.20 equals the quote, there are no ERP gantry lines, no airport surcharge (the trip does not originate at an airport) and a 0.00 waiting-time fee. POL-RD-09(4) therefore finds no phantom line, no standalone refund and no billing-integrity referral.

To the driver: your stated reason ('in this jam') was tested as POL-RD-13 requires, against the only traffic advisory for this trip. That artifact, EV-ADVIS-00715-01, is MISSING, carries no payload and sits at weight_multiplier 0.0 with issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT — I disclose that impairment expressly. Your traffic excuse therefore carries no weight under POL-RD-08 and exonerates nothing. It also does not escalate the case: you cited no advisory identifier, and POL-RD-13(1) provides that the absence of an advisory no party has cited is a gap in the bundle, not a POL-RD-10(5) contradiction.

On the remaining points: the trace is not impaired under POL-RD-07 (100% coverage, 55 fixes at a 10 s cadence, no gaps, max gap 0.0 s), so POL-RD-10(3) and the POL-RD-07(ii) corroboration duty are not engaged. Trip identifiers match across EV-TRIP-00715, EV-GPS-00715 and EV-FARE-00715 and no timestamps conflict, so POL-RD-10(2) and (4) do not fire. No charge line lacks a counterpart in the trace or trip record (POL-RD-10(8)). The profiles were used only where POL-GEN-01 allows: the rider's deviation_claims_60d 0 with deviation_claims_60d_substantiated 0 does not trigger POL-RD-08's corroboration requirement, and the driver's deviation_flags_90d 0 against completed_trips_90d 250 establishes no repeat-deviation pattern, so POL-RD-06 is not engaged and no conduct referral arises. No other profile field was used.

One thing this category cannot reach: the evidence shows the driver ended the trip short and the rider still paid the full upfront charge. The route-deviation clauses provide no remedy for a trip that was not completed, and no escalation trigger fires, so the present state stands. If that non-completion is to be pursued, it is not a route-deviation refund and would have to be raised as the appropriate kind of dispute.

The ruling rests on EV-GPS-00715 and EV-FARE-00715, both weight_multiplier 1.0, so my confidence is 0.85. The contested SGD 7.20 is not refunded and not disturbed.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider and the driver. Both sides' evidence is accepted; the route-deviation tests are run on this trip's own record and neither returns a refund.

DISTANCE. The governing measurement is the GPS trace (POL-RD-01 makes gps_trace.trace_distance_km govern over the rounded trip_record copy, which also reads 3.4 km). The trace was driven 3.4 km against a booked optimal route of 6.4 km, an excess of 3.4 - 6.4 = -3.0 km, or -46.875%. POL-RD-01 establishes a deviation only where the excess exceeds 20% of optimal and 0.8 km absolute; a negative excess clears neither test, so no deviation exists however the trip is characterised. The trace is unimpaired at policy level too: 55 fixes, 100% coverage, 10 s cadence, no gaps, max_gap_sec 0.0, so POL-RD-07 does not bite.

FARE. The fare artifact shows fare_model UPFRONT_QUOTE, quoted_fare_sgd 7.20 and charged_total 7.20. Under POL-RD-11 POL-RD-02 does not run and no distance-or-time refund is available. The only POL-RD-11(a) remedy is the excess of charged_total over the quote plus properly chargeable pass-throughs: 7.20 - 7.20 - 0.00 = 0.00, which the fare artifact itself publishes as pol_rd_11_remedy 0.00. There are no ERP lines (0.00), no airport surcharge (the trip ends at a shelter and does not originate at an airport) and a waiting-time fee of 0.00, so POL-RD-09(4) finds no phantom gantry and issues no billing-integrity referral.

THE INCOMPLETE RIDE. The driver's in-app message of 12:25:40 ('Hospital too far in this jam. I will end here and refund you.') and the trip record's dropoff labelled 'Shelter where service ended' are accepted: they show the journey was ended short of its destination, and the trace's 3.4 km corroborates it. That is not a route deviation, and no route-deviation clause attaches a refund to a trip driven under its optimal distance on an upfront-quoted fare - POL-RD-11 fixes the distance and time charges at booking. The driver's traffic excuse ('in this jam') is asserted with no advisory: the bundle's only traffic_advisory, EV-ADVIS-00715-01, is MISSING (weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT, disclosed), so under POL-RD-08 and POL-RD-13 the assertion carries no weight, and because the driver cited no advisory identifier the absence is not a POL-RD-10(5) escalation trigger.

ESCALATION. No POL-RD-10 trigger fires: identifiers all match TRP-00715; the trace is unimpaired so (3) does not apply; timestamps agree and run forwards; no exculpatory clause is invoked against a cited missing artifact; no POL-RD-02 refund arises; and every fare line has a counterpart. The matter is therefore decidable, and it is decided rather than escalated.

OUTCOME. The claim for a route-deviation refund of SGD 7.20 is not supported and is declined; fare_breakdown.payment_status (CHARGED) and refund_issued_sgd (0.00) stand. One open question is recorded rather than converted into money the policy does not provide: whether an upfront fare should be adjusted when a ride ends early is not addressed by any clause in this policy, and a service-completion route, not route deviation, is where that belongs.

ruling.explanation:
This decision concerns TRP-00715, filed by the rider as a ROUTE_DEVIATION, and the route-deviation rules decide it. To both parties: no route-deviation refund is due.

1. No deviation exists. The booked optimal route was 6.4 km. The GPS trace — which governs over the rounded trip-record copy (POL-RD-01) — shows 3.4 km driven. The excess is 3.4 − 6.4 = −3.0 km, i.e. −46.9%. POL-RD-01 establishes a deviation only where the excess exceeds both 20% of the optimal distance and 0.8 km in absolute terms; a negative excess passes neither test. The trace is unimpaired (100.0% coverage, 55 fixes at 10 s, no gaps, max gap 0.0 s), so this is not a case of missing evidence. POL-RD-01 provides that where either establishment test fails the outcome is NO_ACTION however the rider characterises the trip.

2. The driver's admission is accepted but changes nothing. The in-app message sent 2026-09-24T12:25:40 ('Hospital too far in this jam. I will end here and refund you') and the dropoff label 'Shelter where service ended' show the driver ended the trip early and told the rider a refund was coming. That is evidence the journey was curtailed; it is not evidence of a route deviation (excess distance), and no clause in this policy gives a distance or time refund for a trip driven under its optimal distance. The promised refund is not a remedy any clause of this policy creates.

3. The fare is upfront-quoted and yields nothing under POL-RD-11. charged_total = SGD 7.20, quoted_fare_sgd = SGD 7.20, and the properly chargeable pass-through and statutory lines total SGD 0.00, so the POL-RD-11(a) remedy is 7.20 − 7.20 − 0.00 = SGD 0.00, exactly as the fare artifact publishes (pol_rd_11_remedy 0.00). POL-RD-02 does not run on an upfront trip.

4. There is no pass-through or billing-integrity correction. The fare carries no ERP or toll lines, no airport surcharge (the trip does not originate at an airport) and no waiting-time fee, so POL-RD-09 gives nothing and POL-RD-09(4) finds no phantom gantry and no misplaced surcharge.

5. The driver's traffic excuse carries no weight but is immaterial. The driver cited 'this jam'. The bundle's only advisory, EV-ADVIS-00715-01, is MISSING (weight_multiplier 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT); under POL-RD-13 the excuse is tested against the advisory alone and fails. But with no deviation measured there is nothing for it to excuse, so it does not move the arithmetic. The rider's own arithmetic claim, which itself concedes the route-deviation money clauses return SGD 0.00, is accepted.

6. POL-RD-06 is not consulted, and would not help. It applies only where POL-RD-01 records a MATERIAL deviation, and none is recorded here; in any event driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 250 completed trips in 90 days, so no repeat-deviation pattern is established and no conduct referral arises.

No POL-RD-10 escalation trigger fires: the trip identifiers match (TRP-00715 across trip record, trace and fare), the trace is unimpaired, the timestamps are consistent, the two sides' evidence is not in conflict, and every fare line has a counterpart in the trip record and trace. The contested SGD 7.20 therefore stands, and fare_breakdown.payment_status and refund_issued_sgd are left as they are.

The rider's underlying complaint — that the driver ended the trip short of the hospital — is a real grievance, but it is not a route-deviation matter under this policy, and the route-deviation evidence cannot answer it. That open question is better raised under whatever category addresses a trip ended before its destination; this ruling does not decide it.

All figures are read from EV-TRIP-00715, EV-GPS-00715 and EV-FARE-00715 (each weight_multiplier 1.0).
